name: paper_diffcccg
description: Canonical capacitor cross-coupled differential common-gate LNA: two CG transistors (M1, M2), sources = differential input pair (VIN1/VIN2), drains = differential output pair (VOUT1/VOUT2, each with an inductive load L1/L2); EACH transistor's gate is capacitively cross-coupled (C1, C2) to the OPPOSITE transistor's source/input node (rather than tied to a fixed AC-ground bias), so the differential input swing modulates the gate too -- boosting effective gm without extra bias current. Gate DC bias set via R1/R2 from a shared bias net.
source_family: Capacitor cross-coupled common-gate LNA (differential gm-boosting via cross-coupling, not an auxiliary amplifier stage)

cited_paper.title: A Capacitor Cross-Coupled Common-Gate Low-Noise Amplifier
cited_paper.authors: Weimin Zhuo, Xiaohua Li, S. Shekhar, S.H.K. Embabi, J. Pineda de Gyvez, D.J. Allstot, E. Sanchez-Sinencio (author list per the seminal, widely-cited paper on this technique)
cited_paper.journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs
cited_paper.open_access: NOT independently re-verified this session -- cited from prior knowledge of this seminal, widely-taught paper (referenced across dozens of downstream LNA papers and in RFIC textbooks, e.g. Razavi's RF Microelectronics) plus a confirming web search that surfaced it as 'A seminal work on capacitor cross-coupled common-gate low-noise amplifiers ... published by Zhuo et al. in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II in 2005.' Full text was not fetched.
cited_paper.what_was_actually_read: Web search summary only, confirming the paper's existence, authors (approximate -- see caveat), venue and year, and the one-sentence description of the technique (capacitor cross-coupling of CG devices in a differential cascode LNA to improve gain/NF without extra current). The circuit transcribed here is the textbook description of this well-known technique, not a verified reproduction of this paper's exact figure.

transcription.route: Authored directly in AnalogGenie native format; validated through upstream build_connection_matrix/dfs_all_paths (execed read-only) -> token sequence -> lna/topology.py screen -> lna/to_spice.py -> ngspice.
transcription.notes: This is the only DIFFERENTIAL circuit in this transcription batch (and one of few differential LNAs in the corpus generally -- the existing 41-circuit real-LNA set and this project's own lna/ref/*.cir anchors are predominantly single-ended, per lna/ref/README.md), so it adds a structurally distinct family beyond the 4 single-ended transcriptions alongside it.

transcription_confidence: MEDIUM-LOW on exact author list and bibliographic precision (reconstructed from memory of a well-known paper plus a confirming but non-quantitative web search -- the author list above should be verified before this citation is used in any formal context), MEDIUM-HIGH on the circuit topology itself (the cross-coupling mechanism -- each CG transistor's gate driven by the opposite input via a capacitor instead of a fixed bias -- is the well-established, unambiguous, textbook-documented defining feature of this technique, independently corroborated by multiple related-paper search results describing the same mechanism in near-identical terms).
ambiguous_or_uncertain: Exact author list/page numbers for the 2005 TCAS-II paper were not independently verified via a direct fetch this session -- flagged for review before citing formally.

Whether the source paper's version includes cascode devices above M1/M2 (many real implementations do, for gain/isolation) -- omitted here for a minimal, clean instance of the cross-coupling mechanism itself.
No component values (not sourced); to_spice.py's standard placeholder .param defaults were used.

validation.structural_screen: 5/5 -- all criteria pass (2 inductors / 8 devices = 25% ratio; 8 devices).
validation.ngspice_sim: clean run, op + sp(1-4GHz) + noise, zero errors. S11min=-1.11dB, S21max=-35.8dB with generic placeholder sizing (both differential outputs referenced through the single VOUT1 S-parameter port that to_spice.py sets up; VOUT2 is present as a real node but not part of the 2-port S-parameter setup, same convention as align-lna-qm's VOUT2).

excluded_paper_check: Independent of, and unrelated to, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing. This is a 2005 paper (17 years earlier) on a general differential CG-LNA gm-boosting technique, not a GNSS receiver design.
